text.p: Caterpillar Inc said Tuesday margin as a percent of machinery and engine sales rose to 26.8 percent in the first quarter from 24.5 percent a year ago.

The increase was primarily due to price increases over the past year, higher physical sales volume, a favorable change in geographic sales mix, lower sales discounts and the net effect of the stronger dollar.
The favorable effect of the stronger dollar on costs incurred in Japanese yen and European currencies was substantially offset by the negative impact on prices, Caterpillar said.
Sales inside the United States were $2.17 billion, up 15 percent from a year ago. Sales outside the United States were $1.90 billion, up six percent from a year ago, Caterpillar said.
The provision for income taxes in the quarter was $196 million, up from $143 million a year ago, due to higher before-tax profit and a higher effective tax rate, Caterpillar said.
Physical sales volume in the quarter was up nine percent, while prices improved two percent, Caterpillar said.
The increase in physical sales volume resulted from higher machine and engine sales, Caterpillar said.
Research and development spending in the quarter was $117 million, up $19 million from a year ago, primarily reflecting support of product line expansion.
Earlier Tuesday, Caterpillar reported net income of $394 million, or $2.08 a share, up from $296 million, or $1.53 a share a year ago.
Earnings a share exceeded the mean First Call estimate of $1.69 a share, as well as the $1.85 a share that was the upper range of the analysts surveyed.
